title: surface-retry-signal-with-actor-context-for-multiplexed-tool-streams
author: Maya Chen
body: Summary: Adds a compact, machine-readable retry signal and an accompanying Retry-Actor context header for multiplexed/streamed tool invocations and OpenAI-compat adapter flows. Motivation: existing 429/Retry-After guidance is ambiguous for multiplexed streams and tool/function calls. Consumers and middlewares need an unambiguous, per-invocation retry hint that survives proxies and that can be correlated with the actor that should own any idempotent retry logic. This PR introduces: Retry-Signal header (opaque token or human-friendly hint), Retry-Actor header (string describing the logical actor responsible for retry semantics), and a small extension to the structured error envelope emitted on stream tear-down frames to include RETRY_ADVICE metadata. Design notes: Retry-Signal is designed as an opaque, bounded string token (<= 128 chars) meant for correlation and optional parsing by clients. Retry-Actor is a short identifier (eg: app, job-runner, tool-proxy, user-session) used by SDKs and the OpenAI-compat shim to decide whether client or server should responsibly retry. On streaming responses the runtime will emit a final error frame with ERROR_FRAME that contains RETRY_ADVICE: {type: SOFT|HARD|NONE, wait_ms: integer|null, token: Retry-Signal, actor: Retry-Actor}. For non-streamed HTTP responses we map the same payload into a machine-readable header X-Redwood-Retry and preserve TTL semantics via Retry-After as a human hint. Backwards compatibility and mapping to OpenAI-compat: the adapter keeps returning 429 and Retry-After for user-facing clients but includes X-OpenAI-Compatible-Retry and X-Redwood-Retry headers so proxies and SDKs can use the richer signal when available. Migration: SDKs will be updated to prefer Retry-Signal for automated retries when Retry-Actor matches configured local actors; otherwise SDKs will surface the header to users. Implementation summary: Changes to serving/runtime: - Add retry-advice generator in request router that considers model tolerance, capacity tier, and per-customer rate windows. - Inject Retry-Signal token generation and short-lived lease stored in local cache for correlation. - Populate error frames in stream tear-down path with RETRY_ADVICE envelope. OpenAI-compat adapter: - Include header mapping and compatibility fallback to preserve existing behavior for downstream users. - Add normalization for conflicting Retry-After values by honoring the shortest non-zero wait when present and tagging the token with correlation id. SDKs and client libraries: - Python/TS SDK will accept Retry-Actor policy in config; when actor matches the SDK instance they will perform controlled retries using token and wait_ms; otherwise SDKs expose headers to application. Tests and rollout: unit tests for token generation, integration tests exercising streaming-teardown framing, e2e on the OpenAI-compat shim ensuring legacy clients still see 429+Retry-After. Canary rollout plan: enable on dedicated clusters with traffic split 1% -> 10% -> 50% with metrics tracked: failed request rate after retry, duplicated tool-executions, and idempotency violations. Checklist: - [x] Runtime injection and generator implemented; - [x] Stream error frame extended with RETRY_ADVICE; - [x] OpenAI-compat header mapping implemented; - [x] SDK hooks and docs (draft) included; - [x] Integration tests and CI green. Risks and mitigations: accidental double-execution of tool calls if clients blindly retry. Mitigation: Retry-Actor and Idempotency-Key-Context are required for automatic retries. If actor differs or key missing, SDK will surface a retry advisory instead of retrying. Observability: new metrics added: retry_advice_emitted_total, retry_actor_mismatch_total, retry_token_leases_active. Rollout notes: feature gated behind experimental config 'retry_advice_v1' with safe defaults off for older clusters. See migration guide in docs/ for SDK changes and sample policy snippets. Related: ENG-2103 (retry policy engine), ENG-2104 (stream framing contract).

d4e9a12: add stream error frame RETRY_ADVICE population
f18c3b5: openai-compat header mapping and normalization
b7a8e41: sdk hooks and docs stubs
c9e4a70: tests for streaming teardown and idempotency gating
review_comments: Daniel Park: Please clarify semantics when Retry-After and Retry-Signal disagree. Response: we now select shortest non-zero wait_ms and include decision rationale in metrics.
Sofia Alvarez: Can we enforce token TTL to avoid unbounded cache growth? Response: token leases are capped at 60s and we added eviction metrics.

Priya Natarajan: Add an example of SDK-side policy to avoid duplicate tool execution. Response: included policy snippet in docs/retry_advice.md and SDK add-check to require idempotency-key-context for auto-retry.
QA: Found flake in streaming teardown test when many concurrent streams are closed; fixed race by serializing teardown token issuance in test harness.
release_notes: Introduces Retry-Signal (X-Redwood-Retry / stream RETRY_ADVICE) and Retry-Actor headers to provide unambiguous retry hints for streamed tool invocations. SDKs can optionally perform automated retries when Retry-Actor matches configured actors and an idempotency key context is present. Backwards compatible with existing 429+Retry-After behavior via OpenAI-compat mappings.
notes: This changelist is intentionally conservative: automatic retries are gated on actor/key alignment and the default experimental flag is off for clusters with older client SDKs. Observability hooks and metrics added to detect misconfiguration or unintended duplicate executions.
